key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskites, identifying preferential degradation at the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive degradation screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification improving UV stability in perovskite films and solar cells.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence excitation.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality factor measurements during UV-soaking studies.
Compare perovskite films and p-i-n solar cells with different indium tin oxide interface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localized UV-induced degradation preferentially to the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed reduced damage with silane modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative depth resolution or stability gains, limiting assessment of localization precision and practical benefit.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
